patterns.usage_note: Colloquial contraction of ても/でも: だって appears after ta-stems that voice the た (読んだって, 急いだって) and たって elsewhere (食べたって, 話したって). After a noun it shades into 'even X', close to も. It belongs to everyday speech and is rarely written outside dialogue; the formal counterparts are ても and にしても.

examples.ruby: 素人[しろうと]だって、これがおかしいことくらい分[わ]かる。
examples.english: Even an amateur can tell this much is off.

examples.ruby: そんな記事[きじ]を読[よ]んだって、気分[きぶん]が沈[しず]むだけだよ。
examples.english: Reading articles like that will only get you down.

examples.ruby: いくら考[かんが]えたって、いい案[あん]なんて浮[う]かばない。
examples.english: No matter how hard I think, no good ideas come to me.

patterns.usage_note: A spoken-register 〜としても built on とする + たって: it grants a supposition for the sake of argument, and the main clause typically denies that the supposition changes anything. It attaches to plain forms, including だ and た. Its sibling にしたって picks up an actual case rather than a hypothesis.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]から始[はじ]めるとしたって、準備[じゅんび]がまるで足[た]りない。
examples.english: Even supposing we start tomorrow, we're nowhere near ready.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]が謝[あやま]ったとしたって、そう簡単[かんたん]には水[みず]に流[なが]せない。
examples.english: Even if he did apologize, I can't just let it go that easily.

examples.ruby: 冗談[じょうだん]だとしたって、その言[い]い方[かた]はひどすぎる。
examples.english: Even granting it was a joke, that's a terrible way to put it.

glosses: even in the case of; even for
patterns.usage_note: Colloquial 〜にしても: it singles out a person, group, or case and says the point holds even there. It is most at home after a noun naming someone or some organization ('even X, for their part'), and the following clause is typically negative or concessive. Compare としたって, which grants a hypothesis instead of raising a real case; the formal counterparts are にしても／にしろ／にせよ.

examples.ruby: ベテランの彼[かれ]にしたって、この機械[きかい]は扱[あつか]いにくいそうだ。
examples.english: Even a veteran like him finds this machine awkward to handle, apparently.

examples.ruby: 手伝[てつだ]うにしたって、これだけの量[りょう]は今日[きょう]中[じゅう]に終[お]わらない。
examples.english: Even if I pitch in, there's no finishing this much today.

examples.ruby: うちの部長[ぶちょう]にしたって、この件[けん]は知[し]らされていなかった。
examples.english: Even our own department head, for that matter, was never told about this.

patterns.usage_note: A concessive hypothetical whose main clause almost always says the effort changes nothing (変わらない, 無駄だ, 〜ない), often set up by 今さら/いくら/どんなに. Because the main clause describes how things stand rather than what the speaker will do, commands and requests rarely follow it. The full form is 〜たところで／〜だところで; in casual speech ところ reduces to とこ, giving 走ったとこで, 騒いだとこで. The だ variant appears after ta-stems in ん/い (読んだ, 急いだ).

examples.ruby: 今[いま]から駅[えき]まで走[はし]ったところで、終電[しゅうでん]には乗[の]れない。
examples.english: Even if you sprint to the station now, you're not catching the last train.

examples.ruby: ここで騒[さわ]いだとこで、決[き]まったことはひっくり返[かえ]らないよ。
examples.english: Kicking up a fuss here isn't going to overturn what's already been decided.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]さら言[い]い訳[わけ]を並[なら]べたところで、信用[しんよう]は戻[もど]らない。
examples.english: Piling up excuses at this point isn't going to win back anyone's trust.

patterns.usage_note: An emphatic concessive on the volitional/conjectural form (行こうとも, 険しかろうとも), typically reinforced by たとえ or どんなに. It is written and declamatory in register, stiffer than 〜うと and far stiffer than colloquial ても. Dropping the も gives 〜うと, the same meaning a shade lighter.

examples.ruby: どんなに時間[じかん]がかかろうとも、最後[さいご]までやり抜[ぬ]く。
examples.english: However long it takes, I will see this through to the end.

examples.ruby: たとえ全[すべ]てを失[うしな]おうとも、この信念[しんねん]だけは曲[ま]げない。
examples.english: Even if I lose everything, this one conviction I will not bend.

examples.ruby: 道[みち]がどれほど険[けわ]しかろうとも、彼[かれ]は歩[あゆ]みを止[と]めなかった。
examples.english: No matter how steep the road, he never once stopped walking.

patterns.usage_note: Takes the same volitional attachment as 〜うとも, but が colors it with the speaker's indifference: whatever happens, it makes no difference to me. It is a shade more conversational than うとも and is the form that most readily doubles up (行こうが行くまいが, 雨が降ろうが槍が降ろうが). The main clause commonly states the speaker's resolve or dismissal.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]が反対[はんたい]しようが、この企画[きかく]は必[かなら]ず通[とお]してみせる。
examples.english: I don't care who objects; I'm getting this project approved.

examples.ruby: 上司[じょうし]が何[なん]と言[い]おうが、この方針[ほうしん]は変[か]えるつもりはない。
examples.english: Whatever the boss says, I have no intention of changing this policy.

examples.ruby: 本人[ほんにん]が何[なに]を思[おも]おうが、こちらが口[くち]を出[だ]す筋合[すじあ]いはない。
examples.english: Whatever he chooses to think, it is no place of ours to butt in.

patterns.usage_note: The formal counterpart of 〜にしても; にせよ is stiffer still, and both lean written. Doubled, it lists alternatives and means 'whether … or …'; used singly it concedes a point before the speaker presses an objection or a demand. It attaches to nouns and plain forms, including た. Often after an interrogative (誰にしろ, 何にしろ) meaning 'whoever/whatever', and the singleton use usually leads into a criticism or a demand.

examples.ruby: 賛成[さんせい]するにしろ反対[はんたい]するにしろ、理由[りゆう]は述[の]べてほしい。
examples.english: Whether you're for it or against it, I'd like to hear your reasons.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]にしろ、この程度[ていど]の確認[かくにん]は怠[おこた]るべきでない。
examples.english: Even if you're new here, you shouldn't be skipping a check this basic.

examples.ruby: 知[し]らなかったにしろ、規則[きそく]違反[いはん]は違反[いはん]だ。
examples.english: Even if you didn't know, a breach of the rules is still a breach.
